extracted.intended_audience: GAP developers and library/package authors implementing new objects, representations, and methods
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conventions for creating new GAP object types, representations, and installing methods/operations (arithmetic, comparison, printing, help integration) in the GAP library. Covers implementation details, performance considerations, file/layout conventions, and help-system handler requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison compatibility for finite field elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The comparison < for finite field elements must be compatible with the predefined comparison of the existing finite field element implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manual/documentation lacks details, inspect GAP kernel source code to find the exact comparison behavior. For internally represented finite field elements the comparison is defined in Chapter 59; compatibility may force expensive implementations (e.g., using discrete logs) to match older behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple comparison for ModulusRep nonprime Z/nZ elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For two elements in Z/nZ (ModulusRep, nonprime) a straightforward comparison can be used: compare their stored residue entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example implementation: function(x,y) return x![1] < y![1]; end; This is suitable where elements store the residue at position 1 and no compatibility with other representations is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison for Z/pZ (ModulusRep) via discrete logarithm for compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be compatible with internal finite field element ordering, comparison of Z/pZ (ModulusRep) elements may use discrete logarithms: compute Characteristic(p), get a primitive root r and compare LogMod(x,r,p) < LogMod(y,r,p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces an expensive comparison but ensures compatibility with existing internal FFE ordering. Consider alternative cheaper comparisons only when compatibility is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-type comparisons with internal finite field elements
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing an element in Z/pZ (ModulusRep) with an internal finite field element (FFE), define methods that convert or scale one side appropriately (e.g., multiply the ModulusRep value by One(y) before comparing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: function(x,y) return x![1] * One(y) < y; end and symmetrically function(x,y) return x < y![1] * One(x); end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install same arithmetic methods across representations when compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: Install methods for +, ZeroOp, AdditiveInverseOp, -, *, OneOp, Int, and mod for your ModulusRep objects analogous to those for internal finite field elements when semantics coincide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeat them here if already present for internal types; ensure Int (conversion) is compatible. Be cautious with operations where representation matters (InverseOp, /, ^) and provide additional methods for mixed-representation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide methods for InverseOp, /, and ^ taking representation differences into account
rubrics_metrics.description: For operations whose result or algorithm depends on representation (InverseOp, /, ^), explicitly install methods for combinations of IsMyModulusRep and IsInternalRep to handle mixed-argument cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing such methods can lead to incorrect behavior or errors. Provide methods for (ModulusRep, ModulusRep), (ModulusRep, internal), (internal, ModulusRep) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: DegreeFFE implementation for Z/pZ objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Define DegreeFFE for objects in IsMyZmodpZObj; it need not require IsMyModulusRep since it does not access representation-dependent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: InstallMethod(DegreeFFE, "for element in Z/pZ", [ IsMyZmodpZObj ], z -> 1 );

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerator/Random/Size/Units semantics depend on whether the argument is whole family
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods like Enumerator, Random, Size, Units should assume their argument contains the whole family of elements; thus they make sense only for full-ring (whole-family) objects in nonprime cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prime cases there are existing field methods; for full rings implement Enumerator returning the list of elements (e.g., List([0..Size(R)-1], x -> MyZmodnZObj(F,x))). Units for full ring can be improved to return a group rather than a list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cache MyZmodnZ results to return canonical rings within a session
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent calls MyZmodnZ(n) should ideally return the same ring object for a given n to avoid incompatible rings whose elements cannot interoperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a global list of MyZmodnZ results in the GAP session and return stored values when possible; this also enables PrintObj methods that produce GAP-readable output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units should return a group where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Units (56.5.2) for full rings should preferably return a group object (not merely a list of elements) so the result can be used in group-oriented computations (e.g., SylowSubgroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return a GroupByGenerators result rather than a raw list when possible; e.g., gens := GeneratorsPrimeResidues(Size(R)).generators; return GroupByGenerators(gens, One(R)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Install arithmetic methods to avoid unnecessary intermediate construction
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve efficiency, install methods for -, /, and ^ to handle cases directly instead of relying on constructing additive/multiplicative inverses or intermediate powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of recommended method installations: InstallMethod(-, "two elements in Z/nZ (ModulusRep)", ...); and analogous methods for mixed argument types given in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use the type of an existing object as the first argument of Objectify
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not admissible to take the type of an existing object as first argument to Objectify, because the argument may have knowledge (properties) not correct for the result of an operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if both arguments satisfy IsOne, their sum may not; using an existing object's type can incorrectly propagate properties. Instead, create/remember an appropriate type for results (e.g., store the required type in the family).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate small and large modulus categories for cheaper comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid expensive comparisons for large prime moduli, introduce subcategories (e.g., IsMyZmodpZObjSmall and IsMyZmodpZObjLarge) and install different < methods for these categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install cheaper < implementations for IsMyZmodpZObjLarge when compatibility with internal FFE ordering is not required or internal FFE doesn't cover large sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: New arithmetic operations must be implemented by creating new objects (not by overloading existing ones)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP does not support defining entirely new operations for existing objects (because * and + are already used for canonical meanings); instead create new object types and define the desired operations for those objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: construct LieObject for matrix Lie algebras or FreeMagmaRing for magma rings; use embedding maps to relate original elements to new-object elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare category (filter) and representation for new objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a new filter/category (DeclareCategory or NewCategory) that will return true for your new objects and declare representations (DeclareRepresentation) to describe how internal data are stored (positional/list or record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DeclareCategory("IsMyObject", IsObject); DeclareRepresentation("IsMyObjectListRep", IsPositionalObjectRep, [1]); This allows writing methods matching [ IsMyObject and IsMyObjectListRep ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a new family and type for your objects using NewFamily and NewType
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the family and type your objects belong to and create a constructor (Objectify) using NewType(NewFamily(...), <filters and representation>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store the constructed type in a global variable (MyType := NewType(NewFamily("MyFamily"), IsMyObject and IsMyObjectListRep)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Store immutable copies of underlying data inside objects
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating objects that wrap underlying values, store Immutable(val) to prevent external mutation from changing the wrapped object's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructor: MyObject := val -> Objectify(MyType, [ Immutable(val) ]); prevents changes when the original (e.g., a matrix) is mutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide human-readable and GAP-readable printing via ViewObj and PrintObj
rubrics_metrics.description: Install ViewObj for concise human-readable displays (View) and PrintObj for GAP-readable constructions (Print) so both informal and reproducible outputs are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: InstallMethod(ViewObj, "for object in 'IsMyObject'", [IsMyObject and IsMyObjectListRep], function(obj) Print("<", obj![1], ">"); end ); and InstallMethod(PrintObj, ..., function(obj) Print("MyObject( ", obj![1], " )"); end ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure methods match operation declarations or install appropriate implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations are declared with expected filters (e.g., * declared for IsMultiplicativeElement). A method's argument filters must match the operation declaration; otherwise either use InstallOtherMethod or declare an implication (InstallTrueMethod) so your object's filter implies the operation's required filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer InstallTrueMethod(IsMultiplicativeElement, IsMyObject) to make your objects recognized as multiplicative elements and allow normal InstallMethod to succeed rather than bypassing checks with InstallOtherMethod.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark objects as having inverses when you implement inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: If you implement inverse/One behavior for your objects, install an implication such as InstallTrueMethod(IsMultiplicativeElementWithInverse, IsMyObject) so generic algorithms relying on invertibility become available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also install OneOp and InverseOp (operations) rather than attribute methods if you only handle immutable objects; attributes expect an immutable-return protocol which may not match implementation style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between attributes and operations for One/Inverse implementations
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes (One, Inverse) and their backing operations (OneOp, InverseOp) differ: attributes need to take an object, make it immutable, then return it. For many implementations it's simpler to install OneOp/InverseOp methods directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes that for technical reasons operations OneOp and InverseOp were used instead of attributes in examples because objects are immutable in that design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install equality and ordering methods to enable domain formation and uniqueness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Define = and < for your object type so GAP can form sets/domains and decide uniqueness of neutral and inverse elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: InstallMethod(\=, "for two objects in 'IsMyObject'", ..., function(a,b) return a![1] = b![1]; end); similarly install < using underlying comparison (a![1] < b![1]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare additive-structure implications and install additive methods if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If you also define addition for your objects, declare InstallTrueMethod(IsAdditiveElementWithInverse, IsMyObject) and install methods for +, ZeroOp, and AdditiveInverseOp consistent with your algebraic design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example additive definitions: <a> + <b> = <a+b-1>; ZeroOp returns MyObject(One(a![1])) and AdditiveInverseOp returns MyObject(a![1]/(a![1]-One(a![1]))).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware the mechanism is not suitable for many different multiplications on the same set
rubrics_metrics.description: Installing a new multiplication requires declaring at least one new filter and many methods; thus the design is not ideal if you need many different multiplications on the same underlying set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, once implemented generically (parameterized over the coefficient field), the arithmetic is available for any field F without reimplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP library file naming and purposes (.g, .gd, .gi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library files use suffix conventions: .g for kernel inner workings, .gd for declaration files (categories, attributes, operations, with operation definitions in comments), and .gi for implementation files (method installations, representations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule of thumb .gd files are read before .gi files, so .gi files may assume declarations exist; follow filename case and length conventions (directory names of packages must be lower case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding implementations in the library
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FilenameFunc and StartlineFunc to find the file and starting line of a function definition (with some restrictions), or use method tools to find a method installation. Grep is useful for locating functions and installation strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FilenameFunc does not work, raising the print level of the method-introspection routine (7.2.1) shows the installation string which can be searched in .gi files. Use Browse package tools: BrowseGapMethods and BrowseProfile to navigate implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undocumented variables are unstable—avoid depending on them
rubrics_metrics.description: Global variables not documented in the help system are experimental or minor and may change or be removed; using them in code is risky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need stability, ask at support@gap-system.org for documentation; if the developers decide to document, it will be protected in the manual. Otherwise, include current values in your private code to avoid breakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help-system manual.six format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A manual.six file must start with a line '#SIXFORMAT myownformat' to identify the format; otherwise it is assumed to be the default gapmacro.tex format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ReadSix function for the format will then parse the remainder. If the identifying line is missing, HELP_BOOK_HANDLER.default.ReadSix will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: HELP_BOOK_HANDLER.myownformat.ReadSix return requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ReadSix(stream) must return a record info containing at least bookname (short identifying name) and entries (a list with one entry per searchable string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry of info.entries must be a list whose first element is a string printed by GAP when several matches are found. The info record may contain other components needed by other handler functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required HELP_BOOK_HANDLER functions and SearchMatches contract
rubrics_metrics.description: A help-book handler record HELP_BOOK_HANDLER.myownformat must provide functions including ReadSix, ShowChapters, ShowSection, SearchMatches, MatchPrevChap, and MatchNextChap with specified behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SearchMatches(info, topic, frombegin) must return [exact, match] where exact is indices of exact matches and match the remaining matches; if frombegin true then topic parts separated by spaces are considered word-beginnings, otherwise perform substring search. The topic is normalized (lowercase, whitespace normalized).
